Hi Ben / Clara,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the detailed context on your semantic search use case and the current two-stage pipeline (embedding nearest-neighbor -> heuristic reranker). Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Goal: Replace heuristic reranker with a learned reranker to improve top-5 relevance while keeping tail latency < 120ms for the user-facing path.
- Integration surface: lightweight call after embed+ANN; Redwood reranker API or our hosted ranking model (you can also self-host in Dedicated/Private).
- Key evaluation needs: baseline scoring, candidate set sizes (top_k from ANN), metrics (precision@k, nDCG@k, MRR), and an offline eval harness for A/B.

Next steps we agreed on:
1) You send a sample of queries + gold relevance labels (or a small test set).
2) We share a reranker eval template and sample architecture notes.
3) Engineering sync (30m) to walk SDK/auth and routing options and confirm latency budgets.

I attached the reranker_eval_template.xlsx and a quick architecture sketch.

Proposed engineering sync: Thu 3/19 1pm PT — will loop in Dev (engineering) to go through SDK auth and routing. Does that work?

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — Reranker integration

Hi Ben / Clara — nice to meet you (virtually). Answers and next steps from engineering POV below. TL;DR: we can support both inline synchronous rerank (single API call to /v1/rerank) and async batch scoring; for production low-latency UX we typically recommend top_k between 5-20 for inline; evaluate top_k sweep offline starting from 5, 10, 20, 50.

Auth / SDKs
- Token flows: Redwood supports API keys (current default) and short-lived tokens via our OIDC token exchange integration. For POCs we can enable short-lived service tokens issued by your identity provider (we accept JWTs with standard claims) or issue scoped short-lived tokens from the Redwood Console.
- Node / TypeScript example (pseudo):
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  const res = await client.rerank.rank({ model: 'redwood-reranker-v1', candidates: topCandidates, query });
- Python example for offline eval: we can share a small helper that takes sample_queries.jsonl and returns score vectors for the candidate set.

Routing & Integration Patterns
- Inline synchronous: call reranker as part of the request path. Good when top_k is small (<=20) and you need freshest scores. Expect additional latency = reranker p99 (we'll provide perf numbers for your target model/config).
- Async/background: score candidates offline (or via streaming) and store scores in a fast KV (Redis/elastic). Good when you can tolerate eventual consistency and want lower user latency.
- Hybrid: serve first-pass ANN results immediately; fetch rerank scores and update the UI progressively (progressive enhancement).

Structured output & tool-calling
- Reranker responses include structured metadata fields (score, explanation tokens, feature vector ids). We support optional structured output and tool-calling hooks if you want to trigger downstream actions from high-confidence hits (e.g., launch a support workflow).

Reranker API & payload example
- Endpoint: POST /v1/rerank
- Body: { "model": "redwood-reranker-v1", "query": "...", "candidates": [{"id":"doc1","embedding":[...]}, ...], "top_k": 10 }
- Response: { "ranked": [{"id":"doc7","score":0.92, "explain": "..."}, ...] }

Top_k tuning guidance
- Sweep offline: top_k = [5,10,20,50,100] using your ANN top_100 as candidate source. Measure quality (nDCG@5, precision@5) vs estimated latency (reranker_end_to_end).
- For production: if your latency SLO is <120ms, aim for top_k <= 20 and model quantization (int8) + batching to reduce cost/latency.

Eval metrics & recommendations
- Metrics to compute: precision@k, recall@k, nDCG@k (k=5,10), MRR, and calibration curves for score thresholds. For ranking-specific diagnostics: pairwise loss proxy and average relevance delta vs baseline.
- Dataset splits: train/dev/test with temporal holdout if queries are time-varying. Keep 10-15% for test.
- A/B: run an online A/B test (click-through or human-judged relevance) once offline gains look good.

Attachments & artifacts
- I'm attaching a small architecture diagram and the reranker_eval_template.xlsx Marissa referenced. I also added a sample eval script note in the Drive folder.

Proposed POC steps (engineering):
1) We run an offline sweep on your sample 2k queries (you already shared sample_queries.jsonl).
2) We produce a short report with nDCG@5, nDCG@10, MRR and latency estimates for top_k candidates.
3) Decide inline vs async for the first release and implement a 2-week POC.

I'll be on the 3/19 1pm PT call to demo the SDK and show the reranker request/response.

Hi team — quick follow on the tuning and evaluation side. A few additional recommendations from the ML infra perspective: 

- Evaluation metrics: prioritize nDCG@5 and precision@5 for user-facing UX; report nDCG@10 and MRR as secondary. For binary labels your nDCG is fine — treat labels as graded (1/0) or if you can add a graded relevance label that helps.
- Statistical significance: for offline comparisons use bootstrap sampling or paired t-test on queries for nDCG differences; report 95% CI.
- Label noise: run a small multi-annotator sample to estimate label agreement (Cohen's kappa). If label noise is high, consider active labeling for ambiguous queries.
- Top_k practical guidance: start offline with top_k sweep [5,10,20,50]. If p99 latency at top_k=20 exceeds budget, try quantized model + per-request batching, or move to async.
- Operational monitoring: track per-request latency, score distribution shifts, and degradation on production prompts. We'll set alerting on nDCG drop >3 points.

Proposed timeline:
- 3/19 (today): offline sweep on your sample and quick call to align.
- By 3/24: deliver offline eval report + suggested top_k for POC.
- 2-week POC after alignment.

Happy to discuss tradeoffs on the call.

\u0014Rishi
